scenario_description:
Objective: Finish packing the LM-4627 Spanish/Tagalog delivery pouch for today’s courier batch.
Emerging Need: Packing has begun, but the loaded bundle exceeds the pouch thickness limit and sealing has stopped.
Decision Context: The delivery checklist distinguishes required client documents from an optional generic handbook; the operator can remeasure a compliant bundle before the courier closeout.
Consequence: If no compliant bundle reaches the counter before the batch departs, today’s physical handoff is missed; a later dispatch remains possible.

parameter.title: LM-4627 courier pouch scan window
parameter.description: Front desk courier batch for sealed Spanish/Tagalog delivery pouch; barcode must scan before the counter closes.

parameter.subject: PackStation started LM-4627 pouch TS-8814
parameter.body: Pouch TS-8814 is open for LM-4627. The signed readme, query appendix and completed checklist have been scanned into the pouch log. A spare generic linguist handbook was also placed in the bundle. The operator is checking thickness before sealing; expected ready time is14:55 Pacific.

parameter.content: I am at the front desk: TS-8814 packing has stopped because the bundle measures11 mm but the approved pouch allows at most8 mm. Nothing is trapped or locked; the operator will not force the seal. The spare handbook measures4 mm. The required client-document bundle can be rechecked after a permitted packing change; courier intake ends15:05.

parameter.title: LM-4627 pouch barcode closeout
parameter.content: The courier counter must receive a sealed, operator-checked TS-8814 pouch by15:05. Over-thickness bundles will be retained for later dispatch.

parameter.subject: TS-8814 retained after courier batch departure
parameter.body: The15:05 courier batch has departed. TS-8814 was still over the8 mm pouch limit and was retained unsealed at the secure desk. Its client documents are intact, but they are not on today’s courier run.
